title: Inheritance is one-way and read-time only — private context never lands in a public ledger

tags: [founding, constitutional, privacy]

The personal ledger is private. Repo ledgers ship publicly as part of an OSS
repository. The tier design (dec-0006) puts them in the same graph, so the boundary
has to be enforced by the architecture rather than by care.

Three rules, and they are absolute:

1. **Downward only.** A child ledger may read its parents. A parent is never
   written to by a child, and dira has no verb that does so.
2. **Read-time only.** Inherited context is materialized into a session brief in
   memory. It is never persisted into the child's `.dira/entries/`, so it cannot be
   committed by accident.
3. **No leakage through derived artifacts.** Any entry marked `private: true` — and
   every entry in a `tier = "person"` ledger by default — must not appear in a
   mirrored ADR, an exported view, a hosted render, or a `dira check` message that
   is written to a public path. Where a check needs to cite a private constraint in
   a public context, it cites the **ref only** (`me:cst-0002`), never the text.

The failure this prevents is unrecoverable in the way that matters: a private
strategic note or personal constraint committed into a public repo's git history
cannot be un-published. Treat any violation as a security bug, not a UX bug.
